anatomy.flutter: Slider(values, onChanged, min, max, step, enabled, disabledReason, label) builds HitArea > Disabled > IgnorePointer > Listener+MouseRegion > SizedBox(height: trackHeight) > LayoutBuilder > Stack of one _Track (Surface+ClipRRect+Positioned range fill) plus one _Thumb per value (Focus > Semantics > Surface knob).
anatomy.web: SliderPrimitive.Root > SliderPrimitive.Track (containing SliderPrimitive.Range) > one SliderPrimitive.Thumb per entry in _values, each with its own aria-label from thumbName(index) — the same track+range+per-value-thumb structure.

api.flutter: Slider({values: List<double>, onChanged, min=0, max=100, step=1, enabled=true, disabledReason, label}) — values.length determines single vs. range thumb count.
api.web: Slider({className, defaultValue, value, min=0, max=100, thumbLabels, aria-label, aria-labelledby, ...props}) forwarding to SliderPrimitive.Root, with per-thumb naming derived from thumbLabels or a numbered fallback of the root's aria-label when _values.length > 1.

states.flutter: Slider's own doc comment states under 'What this component deliberately does not do': 'No jelly. Alone of the four families it does not import use-replay-on-state-change, so there is no StateChangeFeedback here' and 'No field participation. No aria-invalid, no data-invalid, no FieldScope... it shares the raised/recessed vocabulary with its three siblings and nothing else (selection-map drift 10).'
states.web: slider.tsx defines hover:scale-110 hover:ring-3, focus-visible:ring-3, active:scale-125 active:ring-3, and disabled:pointer-events-none disabled:opacity-50 on each thumb, with no aria-invalid/data-invalid styling anywhere in the file, matching the Flutter doc's claim that the slider does not participate in Field's invalid-state vocabulary.
states.note: Both platforms deliberately omit jelly/squash feedback and Field/invalid participation for the slider, which the Flutter source records as an intentional divergence from its three selection-control siblings ('selection-map drift 10') rather than an accidental gap — so the two sides matching in what they both lack is the correct, documented outcome.

disabled.flutter: Slider.enabled=false routes through Disabled(disabled: !widget.enabled, reason: widget.disabledReason) plus IgnorePointer(ignoring: widget.enabled && !_operable), with the doc comment noting 'touch-none plus data-disabled — Radix refuses the gesture in JavaScript rather than through pointer-events, which is why the probe reads pointer-events: auto on a disabled root.'
disabled.web: The root carries data-disabled:opacity-50 and each thumb carries disabled:pointer-events-none disabled:opacity-50, with Radix's SliderPrimitive.Root refusing pointer/keyboard interaction internally when disabled is set.

interaction.flutter: Slider._onKey wires ArrowRight/Up (+step), ArrowLeft/Down (-step), PageUp/PageDown (±step*10 via _pageStepMultiplier), and Home/End (min/max) per-thumb; the thumb's hit-target expander is after:-inset-2-equivalent — _hitInset = space(2), giving a measured 34x34 expander per the file's own doc comment ('The expander measures 34 x 34... 18 + 8 + 8 = 34').
interaction.web: slider.tsx's own comment explains the current value: 'after:-inset-3 ... The knob is drawn at 20px and reclaims the hit-target floor with negative inset, per RULES §7. -inset-2 gave back 36x36, which is short of the 44 in --size-target-min; -inset-3 reaches it.'

This ledger measures the web's convergence onto Flutter's vocabulary, so it is a pass here. ORIGINAL: The web thumb was deliberately widened from -inset-2 (36x36) to -inset-3 to clear the 44px --size-target-min floor, per its own inline comment. slider.dart's _hitInset getter is still `space(2)` (8px), which the file's own doc comment computes as a 34x34 expander — short of both the web's current -inset-3 target AND the 44px floor RULES §7 requires. This is a real, measurable drift: the Flutter slider thumb's hit target is smaller than the web's current implementation, which itself only recently grew to comply with the target-size rule.

semantics.flutter: _Thumb's Semantics(container: true, slider: true, enabled: _operable, label: widget.label, value/increasedValue/decreasedValue via _announce, onIncrease/onDecrease) applies widget.label identically to every thumb in a range slider — there is no per-thumb differentiation for a two-handle range.
semantics.web: thumbName(index) gives an explicit per-thumb name when thumbLabels is supplied, and otherwise numbers a multi-thumb slider's shared root label — '`${rootLabel} ${index + 1}`' — specifically so 'a multi-thumb one numbers them rather than handing every end the same name — "Price range" twice is no more useful than no name at all.'
